findings.excerpt: In a commutative $3 \times 3$ diagram, suppose the middle row and middle column are short exact. If any three of the remaining four rows and columns are short exact, then the fourth is short exact. / **Given:** The commutative $3 \times 3$ diagram in the statement.
findings.symptom: The statement and given-data line refer to a 3×3 commutative diagram, but the rendered ItemBody contains no diagram, vertices, or arrows. This leaves the nine exactness hypotheses and the four possible missing outer lines to be inferred.
findings.suggested_repair: Editorial candidate: include a generic 3×3 diagram with named objects and horizontal/vertical arrows, and make clear that the middle row and column are short exact while any three outer rows/columns are short exact. Keep the arrows commutative and the statement symmetric under transpose and opposite-category reversal.

The source-supported checks are exactness of both rows and the two four-lemma implications; coordinate the displayed shape with the linked module and abelian-category statements.
